name: aws_security_group
description: Provides a security group resource. Security groups act as a virtual firewall for your EC2 instances, EKS nodes, RDS instances, and other AWS resources to control inbound and outbound traffic. Security groups are stateful: if you send a request from your instance, the response traffic is allowed regardless of inbound rules.
use_cases: Control inbound/outbound traffic to EC2 instances and EKS nodes
Restrict database access to application layer only
Allow ALB to communicate with backend services

optional.name: name
optional.description: Name of the security group. If omitted, Terraform will assign a random unique name.

optional.name: description
optional.description: Security group description. Defaults to 'Managed by Terraform'. Cannot be empty string.

optional.name: vpc_id
optional.description: VPC ID where the security group is created. Defaults to the region's default VPC.

optional.name: ingress
optional.description: Ingress rules. Deprecated in favor of aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule resource for better state management.

optional.name: egress
optional.description: Egress rules. Defaults to all traffic allowed. Deprecated in favor of aws_vpc_security_group_egress_rule.

optional.name: tags
optional.description: Map of tags to assign to the resource.

best_practices: Use aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule and aws_vpc_security_group_egress_rule resources instead of inline rules for better state management
Never use 0.0.0.0/0 for inbound rules on sensitive ports (DB, admin ports)
Prefer source security group references over CIDR blocks for internal communication
Add descriptive comments to each rule so purpose is clear
Use separate security groups for each tier (ALB, App, Database)
Restrict SSH/RDP access to specific IP ranges or use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager
Apply the principle of least privilege: only open ports that are actually needed
security_notes: NEVER open port 22 (SSH) or 3389 (RDP) to 0.0.0.0/0 — use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager instead
Security groups are stateful — outbound rules automatically allow return traffic
Use VPC Flow Logs to audit what traffic is actually flowing through security groups
Regularly audit security group rules and remove unused rules

common_errors.fix: Use aws_security_group_rule resource or reference security group IDs via variables

common_errors.error: Cannot delete security group: it is associated with another resource
common_errors.fix: Remove all EC2 instances and other resources from the SG before deletion
